changes: packages/main/src/handlers/worktree.ts: dev_finish/dev_merge now delegate to runStoryTransition (raw-actor phase writes removed; messages corrected). packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts: uniform per-story transition lock for ALL phases + ATOMIC mkdir persist-claim across the synchronous re-read->write (the authoritative double-mint fence; IDEA->PLAN checklist write happens inside it). packages/main/src/core/story-transition-lock.ts (new): advisory git-common-dir-anchored transition lock with liveness classifier and in-process fail-fast guard. packages/main/src/core/mkdir-lock.ts: universal ownership-checked release via atomic rename-verify-restore + ownedAuxFiles cleanup + requireHolderToken fail-closed. Per-story runtime locks (checklist/finding/review-run/init-check/prompt-envelopes/process-events) relocated from committed story metadata to gitignored .lattice/locks/. hints.ts + dev_start/dev_merge texts corrected. transition-integrity-smoke.ts: 79 checks incl. real two-process races.
usage: Normal lifecycle: lattice story_advance --storyId=B-x --phase=REVIEW (or the dormant dev_finish/dev_merge handlers) — transitions now mint exactly one review round and one phase_transition event even under same-owner concurrency; a concurrent attempt aborts with 'concurrent transition already advancing/advanced'. Verify with: node packages/main/dist/tasks/transition-integrity-smoke.js
expectedOutcome: dev_finish/dev_merge route through the canonical runStoryTransition orchestrator (review round minted, phase_transition event carries the real target, no TEST mislabel), and two concurrent same-owner transitions from the same phase produce exactly one committed transition with the loser aborting cleanly.
actualTranscript: transition-integrity smoke: 79/79 checks deterministic (5x) - dev_finish lands REVIEW with a minted review round and correct phase_transition event; dev_merge delegates TEST->DONE; two REAL concurrent processes racing DEV->REVIEW with the advisory lock BYPASSED yield exactly one commit (atomic mkdir persist-claim aborts the loser). heartbeat + quorum smokes green; RED harness GREEN; lattice validate PASS 6/6 must intents. 8 cross-host review rounds converged: final round all 4 lanes PASS (genuine codex host-B + 3 claude lanes), quorum full-3x2 recorded on the merged tree.
outcomeDiff: No difference — expected and actual match on every assertion. The KNOWN LIMITATION documented in-code describes a theoretical multi-second OS-freeze scenario that was never observed in any test.
limitations: The atomic persist-claim uses a time-based stale reclaim (staleMs=15000), so a holder frozen at the OS level (SIGSTOP-class) for longer than staleMs mid-persist could theoretically be reclaimed while alive; the persist critical section is fully synchronous, which makes runtime-level preemption of a live holder impossible, and this boundary is documented in-code as a KNOWN LIMITATION in story-transition-lock.ts and transition-orchestrator.ts. A doubly-degenerate concurrent-release race can leave a bounded, self-healing lock-dir artifact that the normal stale-reclaim path collects (smoke CHK-002d4 proves the bound). Hardening the claim with fencing tokens (a monotonic generation checked at commit, with crash recovery) is planned as its own future story, already tracked and started by the maintainer.
pitfalls: 8 cross-host review rounds were needed: the mutex went through three architectures (held mkdir lock -> read-then-write CAS -> atomic mkdir persist-claim) because a filesystem advisory lock alone cannot be a correctness fence — genuine codex host-B and the quality lane repeatedly REPRODUCED double-mints the other lanes missed. Universal lockId tokens initially dirtied git-tracked story dirs (holder.json committed mid-hold broke quorum-submit-smoke clean-tree; fix = relocate locks to .lattice/locks/ + gitignore **/*.lock/). Non-recursive release initially leaked dirs containing heartbeat.json (ownedAuxFiles fix). A sibling story landing on main mid-review touched two shared files and forced a merged-state re-verification round plus a fresh quorum; it also grew quorum-submit-smoke past the default 270s validate budget (356s at idle), which blocked every story's gate until lattice.config.json pinned that command at 600s. scope_contract_acknowledge --paths=a,b,c stores ONE comma-joined string — ack files individually. summary_set requires changes/usage/limitations/pitfalls too; JSON form works.
